source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"The crutch pad is about 1 to 1.5 inches below the axilla, the elbows are slightly flexed, and body weight is supported through the hands only.","B":"The crutch pad is pressed firmly into the axilla, the elbows remain fully extended, and most body weight is supported through the armpits.","C":"The crutch pad is level with the axilla, the handgrips are set below wrist level, and body weight is transferred through the axillary pads.","D":"The crutch pad is several inches above the axilla, the elbows are locked straight, and forward movement is produced by leaning on the armpits."}}
source_row.rationale: Axillary crutches are fitted with space between the axilla and the crutch pad—about 1 to 1.5 inches (roughly two to three finger widths)—with slight elbow flexion. Body weight should be borne through the hands, not the axillae, to reduce neurovascular compression.
source_row.source_detail: MedlinePlus Using Crutches, fitting instructions: top of crutch 1–1.5 inches below armpit; support weight on hands rather than armpits. NIH MedlinePlus current patient instructions reviewed 2026-08-15. Reviewed 2026-08-15.
